title: Recycled and Hydraulically Stabilised Layers in a Circular Accelerated Pavement Test: Three-Dimensional Finite Element Evaluation of Five Pavement Structures
content: Reclaimed asphalt pavement (RAP) and soils or aggregates stabilised with hydraulic binders are increasingly used in road bases, but comparisons under the same load are scarce. A three-dimensional finite element model of the ALT-LIRA circular accelerated pavement test facility, verified against layered elastic solutions, was used to evaluate five sectors: an unbound crushed-stone base, a RAP base and a gravel base stabilised with a hydraulic binder, and two thicker structures with a stabilised clay capping layer. Under a 57.5 kN dual wheel, the model reproduced the layered elastic asphalt strain within 3.2% and the subgrade strain within 4.3%, whereas the surface deflection was 29–44% smaller because of the rigid pit. Stabilising the base reduced the asphalt strain by 54%. The tensile stress at the bottom of the RAP layer reached the splitting tensile strength (ratio 1.02), against 0.57 for the gravel layer and 0.18 or less in the thicker structures; a loss of asphalt stiffness of 50% raised the RAP ratio to 1.10. Sliding of the asphalt package increased the asphalt strain by 1.6–3.4 times and was the largest uncertainty. The model did not reproduce the measured ranking of the asphalt strains of the five structures.
